findings.text: the third plasma shot E101173 is counted among the three plasma shots carrying the raw MDAC loops and probes, but its store /work/projects/imas_gpu/jt60sa/101173.zarr holds all 34 magFlxLp loops and zero of the 23 magPbTC probes (verified by enumerating the store's MDAC category: 34 loops, no magPbTC arrays), while its commit body 1331cb48 and the fragment's summary both assert it holds magPbTC1..23. The node's own MDAC census (scratch/mdac_presence.json) records 23/23 probes present in the EDDB MDAC catalogue for E101173, so the probes were fetchable with one fetch_channels call; the manifest follow_ons flags a similar E100595 channel gap but not this one, so the gap is unreported. Result: only two of the three plasma examples (E100658, E101154) carry loops and probes.

E101173 has no PSRC/Ip store (its table row reads 'absent (irc 1015)'), so by the fragment's own plasma criterion ('real Ip waveform') it does not qualify as a plasma example and the classifier returns no verdict for it; the census lists E100666 and E101035 as plasma candidates carrying a real Ip waveform that it did not cache, so a genuine third plasma shot was available alongside the one it counted.

The node is an evidence-only census: it enumerates the JT-60SA EDDB over ssh -F ~/.ssh/config jt-60sa, tables every candidate pulse carrying the raw MDAC loops magFlxLp1..34 and probes magPbTC1..23 with its series, date, peak PSRC/Ip, peak PF coil currents, TF current and polarity, and catalogue range, and caches three vacuum shots (E100595, E100579, E100642) and three plasma shots (E100658, E101154, E101173) under /work/projects/imas_gpu/jt60sa through fetch_channels. This reviewer re-derived the fragment's table from the run's own raw census JSON, enumerated the six cached zarr stores for their channel membership and byte sizes, ran the node's own vacuum classifier, and read the per-request fetch receipts. Nothing ran on GPU; the checks are zarr directory reads and one-second python probes.
